We feel that when the war is disposed of, an event of this nature, held on one of our best tracks, would attract an embarrassingly large entry, and do much to popularise walking as a sport. 1, F.
In a batch at about 5 miles were Jack Bidgood, Charlie Churcher and Fred Redman, all walking very strong. At 18 miles Charlie started to drop back and Jack Rutland came up.

Our walkers were soon seen to be prominent, with Harry Churcher and Fred Redman, of the Metropolitan W.C., contesting the lead. Round about three miles, Harry broke away up the hill and proceeded to build up a big lead.
